Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 1–7 (part 1 of 2):

Alif-Lam-Mim (1 – 7)

The surah opens with the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters). This points to the fact that the Qur'an and this surah are composed of the same letters that lie within the reach of the Arabs, yet despite this the Qur'an and this surah are inimitable. To this day they have been unable to produce speech of this kind. These letters of the alphabet belong to their own language, and they are able to form words and speech from them.

After this comes the truthful historical prophecy in which it was said that the Romans would again prevail within a few years. Ibn Jarir, with his chain of narration, reports from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that the Persians were dominant over the Romans, and the Arab polytheists wished that the Persians would remain dominant over the Romans, while the Muslims did not wish that the Persians would prevail over the Romans. This was because the Romans were People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), and they were closer to the minds of the Muslims. When this verse was revealed:

Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearby land, and after their defeat they will prevail within a few years (30: 1 – 4). The polytheists of Makkah said, "Abu Bakr! Your companions say that the Romans will prevail within a few years' term." Abu Bakr wagered four she-camels on it. Seven years passed and nothing happened. The polytheists rejoiced greatly at this, and this was displeasing to the Muslims. They mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said, "What is the meaning of bid' sinin (a few years) in your language?" They said, "Fewer than ten." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) to go and extend the term by two years. It is said that before two years had passed, riders came and reported that the Romans had prevailed over Persia. Upon this the Muslims rejoiced greatly.

Many narrations have come concerning this. Of them, we have adopted the narration of Imam Ibn Jarir. Before we move beyond this event, it is necessary to reflect on the guidance contained in it.

The first lesson for us in this event is that shirk and kufr are one community in every time and place, and they have always been opposed to faith and the belief in Tawhid. Although in that era the mutual ties between the governments of the world were not as deep as in our era, nevertheless the polytheists of Makkah considered that the dominance of the polytheists throughout the world was their dominance, and the victory of the polytheists over the People of the Book was their victory. The Muslims of Makkah also believed that there was a basis of connection between them and the People of the Book, and they too did not like that the polytheists should gain dominance over the People of the Book anywhere. The Muslims believed that their call and movement could not remain isolated in this world, and that external events could influence this struggle between kufr and iman.

This is the plain reality which most people of our era are heedless of, and they cannot understand this reality in the way that the Muslims of the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) understood it, although fourteen hundred years have passed. Today's Muslims think only in terms of the reform of geographical boundaries or nationality, whereas the real issue is that of kufr and iman, and the true battle is between Hizb Allah and Hizb al-Shaytan.

It is necessary that the Muslims of the whole world understand the real nature of this struggle: what the real issue is. If the Muslims have understood the real issue, then the groups carrying the banners of kufr and shirk, which they have raised in various colours, will not be able to deceive the Muslims. These people wage war against the Muslims solely because of the Islamic way of life. Whatever the apparent causes and factors of the conflict may be, the real war is one of ideas.

The second lesson in this event is to rely upon the promise of Allah, as Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) immediately said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had spoken the truth, while in the view of the polytheists this statement of the Messenger (ﷺ) was astonishing. Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) plainly said, "They have spoken the truth." They made the wager and Abu Bakr accepted it, and what Allah had said, that this event would occur within a few years, came to pass. It was this firm confidence, certainty and trust that filled the hearts of the Muslims with conviction and steadfastness, and they bore all trials and hardships cheerfully, until the word of Allah was fulfilled and the promise of Allah was proven true. This is the best weapon of a committed ideological worker on the long path of jihad.

The third lesson is given in the midst of the narration of this event through a very brief parenthetical remark. Allah says: "To Allah belongs the command, before and after" (30: 4). It was said very swiftly that all affairs are in the hands of Allah. This applies to this event and to other events as well. This is a principle, the criterion of the Islamic position. Victory and defeat, the rising and falling of governments in the world, gaining strength and becoming weak, occur in the same way as other natural events occur in this universe. A sunnah (established law) has been fixed for all of them. This sunnah is in the hand of Allah, and He turns the course of events as He wills. All this takes place by the will and wisdom of Allah. All events and occurrences are in truth manifestations of the absolute will of Allah, and no one has any power to determine their direction. No one has the strength. Nor does anyone know the wisdom behind these events except Allah. No one knows the source and beginning of these events, nor their end. Therefore the safe path for a human being is to submit before Allah regarding all events and to say that this is the destiny decreed by Allah.

"Alif-Lam-Mim... by the help of Allah..." (30: 1 – 5): The Romans have been defeated in the nearby land, and after their defeat they will prevail within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory granted by Allah (30: 1 – 5). And the promise of Allah was true, and the believers rejoiced in the help that Allah gave.

"He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful" (30: 5). In short, all authority belongs to Allah, before and after. Allah grants victory to whomever He wills. His will is not restricted by anything. His will, whatever outcome it desires, also provides the causes that bring it about. There is no contradiction between the existence of causes and the attachment of victory and success to the will of Allah. The laws of nature that govern this world of causes are all provided by the absolute will. It is the divine will that has decided that such causes and such sunan should operate among the people of the world, which are unalterable, and that there should be order and stability in this universe. Therefore defeat and victory also appear as a result of natural causes and influences, in accordance with the laws of nature established by Allah.

On this subject, the Islamic way of life is very clear, reasonable and logical. It entrusts all matters to Allah, yet Islam does not deny the world of causes, and it commands man to continue his struggle within the world of causes, so that the results ordained by Allah come into the realm of manifestation. Whether results appear in practice in accordance with human struggle or not, man is not responsible for that. Struggle is obligatory upon him. The outcome is in the hand of Allah. A Bedouin once left his she-camel loose at the gate of the Prophet's Mosque (ﷺ), entered to pray, and said, "I have put my trust in Allah" (tawakkaltu 'ala Allah). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Tie her and then put your trust (i'qilha wa tawakkal)." In the Islamic way of life, trust in Allah comes after struggling within the world of causes, in accordance with the causes. Struggle, and then leave the matter to Allah.

"Allah grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful" (30: 5). This victory is enveloped in the shadows of divine power, and it is this divine power that brings this disposition into the actual world. Over this victory the shadows of divine mercy also spread, through which the interests of people take the form of reality. For the oppressed and downtrodden classes there are many benefits in this.

"And if Allah had not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would certainly have been corrupted" (2:251). Reform of the earth can be achieved only by supporting the oppressed and downtrodden and by treating them with sympathy.

"This is the promise of Allah; Allah does not break His promise, but most people do not know. They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, and they are heedless of the Hereafter" (30: 6 – 7). This is the promise of Allah, so it will certainly come to pass.

"Allah does not break His promise" (30: 6). Because the promise of Allah stems from His unrestricted will, it contains profound wisdom, and He has the power to make His promise a reality. No power can oppose His will, and no one can disobey His command. In this whole universe only what Allah wills takes place. The fulfilment of this promise is in truth a part of Allah's vast law of nature, and within the majesty of Allah's order, His law of nature and His great cosmic plan, no alteration or change is possible.

"But most people do not know" (30: 6). Although it may apparently seem that they wear great turbans and robes and possess a great quantity of knowledge, their knowledge is superficial and relates to the outward affairs of life. They do not know the unalterable laws of nature of Allah, the true principles of this universe, its great order, and its very firm and profound connections.

"They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world" (30: 7). They make no effort to look behind this outward appearance, nor do they try to perceive its background with insight. This outward world is trivial and insignificant. Although it appears to people to be very vast, in reality it is very small. A human being struggles greatly in this world, but in the limited life of a human being very little can be accomplished here, and this limited life is, compared with the vastness of this great universe, only a small portion of it. And this life too is governed by the same laws that govern the whole universe.

A person whose conscience and heart are not connected with the universe, and who has no sense that this universe is controlled by unalterable laws of nature, such a person may indeed be looking at this universe outwardly, but he is like a blind man. He sees outward forms; he sees that everything here revolves in circles, yet he is unable to grasp the reality of this motion. Therefore he is not truly present in this world, nor is he with it. Most people are of this kind, because the true believer is one who is acquainted with this universe and with the secrets and mysteries of life within it. It is such a believer who truly gives to knowledge and science a spirit that perceives realities. People who hold this kind of faith are few in this world. This is why the majority are veiled from true recognition.

"And they are heedless of the Hereafter" (30: 7). The Hereafter is a link in the chain of this universe's existence. The Hereafter is a page of the book of the cosmos. Those who do not understand the reality of creation, who do not understand the natural laws found in this universe, do not understand the Hereafter either. Therefore they do not attach importance to the Hereafter, they make no preparation for it, and they do not understand that on the line of the universe's movement the Hereafter is also a point. This world and this universe are destined to reach that point, and after it a new journey begins.

But as a result of heedlessness of the Hereafter, the values of such heedless people become unsettled; there is no stability or firmness in their values of life. Their conception of life, their interpretation of events, and their standards of worth are immature. Their knowledge is superficial, deficient and outward. For when a person accepts the establishment of the Hereafter at the end of this whole life, his viewpoint on all the events of this world changes. He sees that his life in this world is a brief stage, and that his share in this world, and what it ought to be, is very minor and insignificant compared with the Hereafter, and that the whole life of this world is in truth a very brief show or glimpse of the longest drama. Therefore it is not proper for anyone to pass judgment by looking only at the briefest glimpse of this longest drama. If someone judges the whole of life, the whole universe, and the Hereafter and its long life by looking at a most insignificant glimpse, that will be a superficial judgment.

It is for this reason that a person who believes in the Hereafter and is preparing for it cannot live together in harmony with a person whose outlook is limited to this world and who has no goal beyond it. Two such people can agree neither on any programme for this world nor on any value. The measures of both will be entirely different. In short, in every event, every situation, and every circumstance of life, the judgement of the two will differ, because their scales are different. Each has a different point of view, and each has a different light. Consequently, each sees the same thing differently. Their conception of events, values and circumstances will be distinct. One looks at things with the outward gaze of this world, while the other, with a deep insight, also perceives the background of events. He sees the apparent causes and events, and his attention is also on the hidden inner reality. He knows both the apparent and the unseen. He knows both this world and the Hereafter, and knows the reality of both life and death. He holds the conception of past, present and future. He is aware of the realm of humankind and also knows the other worlds of this universe, and is acquainted with the living and the dead alike. This is that wide horizon upon which Islam focuses the vision of human beings, and it gives them a perspective that befits humankind, that is necessary for the human being as the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and that the spirituality which Allah has deposited in the personality of man also demands.

For this purpose, the promise of Allah's help is a truth in the same way that this orderly universe stands upon a great truth, and that the establishment of the Hereafter is the necessary consequence of this great reality. Now the context of the discourse again takes us on a tour of the inner world of this universe: in the heavens, in the earth, and in the worlds that lie between them. After this, the human being is again taken on a tour of his own existence, so that they may reflect, and perhaps they may arrive at that supreme reality from which they are now heedless, for they are heedless of the Hereafter. Because of a superficial outlook, they cannot even grasp the reality of the Islamic call, since this call is founded upon that great truth and its deep reflection.

Therefore they do not attach importance to the Hereafter, they make no preparation for it, and they do not understand that on the line of the universe's movement the Hereafter is also a point. This world and this universe are destined to reach that point, and after it a new journey begins.

But as a result of heedlessness of the Hereafter, the values of such heedless people become unsettled; there is no stability or firmness in their values of life. Their conception of life, their interpretation of events, and their standards of worth are immature. Their knowledge is superficial, deficient and outward. For when a person accepts the establishment of the Hereafter at the end of this whole life, his viewpoint on all the events of this world changes. He sees that his life in this world is a brief stage, and that his share in this world, and what it ought to be, is very minor and insignificant compared with the Hereafter, and that the whole life of this world is in truth a very brief show or glimpse of the longest drama. Therefore it is not proper for anyone to pass judgment by looking only at the briefest glimpse of this longest drama. If someone judges the whole of life, the whole universe, and the Hereafter and its long life by looking at a most insignificant glimpse, that will be a superficial judgment.

Two such people can agree neither on any programme for this world nor on any value. The measures of both will be entirely different. In short, in every event, every situation, and every circumstance of life, the judgement of the two will differ, because their scales are different. Each has a different point of view, and each has a different light. Consequently, each sees the same thing differently. Their conception of events, values and circumstances will be distinct. One looks at things with the outward gaze of this world, while the other, with a deep insight, also perceives the background of events. He sees the apparent causes and events, and his attention is also on the hidden inner reality. He knows both the apparent and the unseen. He knows both this world and the Hereafter, and knows the reality of both life and death. He holds the conception of past, present and future. He is aware of the realm of humankind and also knows the other worlds of this universe, and is acquainted with the living and the dead alike. This is that wide horizon upon which Islam focuses the vision of human beings, and it gives them a perspective that befits humankind, that is necessary for the human being as the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and that the spirituality which Allah has deposited in the personality of man also demands.

Do these people not think? Their own structure, their own creation, and this vast universe that surrounds them all bear witness that this existence stands upon a truth, and that it moves in accordance with an unshakable natural law (nawamis-i-fitrat) in which there is no disorder. It does not happen that this universe tilts at one time in one direction and at another time in another. Its rotation does not change, the celestial bodies do not collide, and its movement is not a random, blind movement. Nor does this movement change according to shifting desires. Rather, this movement proceeds according to an extremely profound, precise and wise system.

This truth, according to which human life and this vast universe move, demands that this world have an end, where reward and punishment can be fully realized, where good and evil can both receive their due recompense. It is evident that here everything reaches a determined end; this is in accordance with a governing wisdom (hikmat-i-mudabbirah), and every event in this universe appears at its appointed time. There is no advancing or delaying in it.

﴿Indeed, many of the people are, in the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.﴾ (30:8)

The "universe" (zamir-i-kainat) and the vast journey among the creatures existing between the heavens and the earth, which is an extremely wide journey whose horizons are very long and broad and have unimaginable expanses, and within these horizons is a diverse creation, consisting of living and non-living, various kinds of things, including celestial bodies, spheres, stars and planets, large and small stars, the apparent and the hidden, the near and the distant, the known and the unknown. **Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah Al-Rum (30), verses 12–16**

﴿And the Day the Hour is established...to be brought forth into punishment﴾ (12–16)

This is the hour that people are heedless of, and that deniers deny. Look, it has come, and look at its scene. This is the Hour that has been established. Thus a separation is made between the people of faith and the people of disbelief, and their paths part.

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be made happy in a garden﴾ (30:15): "Those who believed and did righteous deeds will be delighted in a garden." There they will encounter a situation in which they will rejoice. Gladness will arise in their consciences, and their hearts will attain joy.

﴿As for those who disbelieved, denied Our signs, and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought forth into punishment﴾ (30:16): "Those who disbelieved, denied Our signs and denied the meeting of the Hereafter will remain present in punishment." This is the final end of the righteous and the wicked.

Now, having taken a tour of the scene of the Hereafter, we return to this world. The journey through this universe, through life within it, and through its secrets, marvels and wonders begins. Indeed, this universe is a fascinating place of recreation. The journey begins with praise of Allah at morning and evening, so look at the morning and evening scenes, how captivating they are.

﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning. To Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and glorify Him in the late afternoon and when you enter the noon. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and gives life to the earth after its death. Thus you will be brought out.

And among His signs is that He created you from dust, and then, behold, you are human beings spreading throughout the earth.

And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.

And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the differences in your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those who have knowledge.

And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear.

And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, producing fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.

And among His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you once from the earth, suddenly you will come forth. To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him. And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (17–27).

This is a deep and grand journey of study through this universe, from its farthest distances to its depths. The faculty of human observation is shown the scenes of morning and evening, and beyond morning and evening, the world of midday. In these horizons and scenes, displays of life, death, spring and autumn are shown. In these pleasant surroundings, a person is told to reflect upon his own creation, to observe the inclinations and tendencies of his nature, and to look at his physical and spiritual powers and their conflict. In this world, everything is in pairs. Observe the mutual affection of these pairs, and look at the inclinations and tendencies of spouses and the powers of their natures. Look at the heavens and earth of this universe, its gardens and wilderness, its colors and order, then the forms of human beings, their colors, and their thousands of languages; then human wakefulness, alertness, sleep, struggle and rest; then the storms, winds, rain, lightning and clouds in this natural universe; then people's love for these and their fear of them; then the deadness and the growth of the earth, and then life and spring. And finally, the establishment, motion and organization of this universe as a whole: who other than Allah can do all this? It is Allah whose manifestations these are. All these tasks are very easy for Him. He is the One who created these things, and He is the One who will recreate them, and recreation is very easy for Him. In the heavens and the earth there are sublime witnesses to the Divine Being, which are unparalleled.

This passage is from Sayyid Qutb's commentary, and the verses it comments on are 30:17–18. Here is the translation:

The command to glorify God and the praise that come after the scenes of the Resurrection described in the preceding phrases and verses, in which it was stated that the people of faith will be joyful in a special garden of Paradise, while the disbelievers and those who denied will be presented before punishment and chastisement. This glorification is brought here in fact as a conclusion, and the earlier scenes of the Resurrection were in truth a preamble to this study of the cosmos: that this vast universe with its rises and falls, the human self with its psychology and wonders, and this creation of God with its secrets and mysteries, are all not purposeless. Consequences of the Resurrection will be established upon them. Therefore there is complete connection and harmony between the earlier scenes of the Resurrection and the present study of the cosmos.

Here, certain times have also been fixed for glorification and praise: in the evening hours, and in the scenes of the morning, in the late afternoon and at the first part of the day. Then this praise and glorification has also been joined with the horizons of the heavens, so that by removing the distances of time and space this praise and glorification may be made all-encompassing, and so that the human heart may remain attached to God at every time and in every place. By observing the structure of this universe, the revolution of the celestial spheres, and the phenomena that arise from them, the phenomena of morning and evening, a person should remember Allah at every moment. His heart should remain open, sensitive, and awake to his surroundings. He should keep observing the environment amid his changing circumstances, and this reflection should continue together with the praise and glorification of Allah. And he should regard all these matters as the signs and miracles of Allah and the Creator of the universe. All these conditions, all these phenomena, and all these times are in fact a miracle of the Lord.

"Yukhriju al-hayya..." through "wa kadhalika takhrujun" (30:19)

"He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living." And this is a continuous process, a process that never stops. There is not a moment in which it pauses. Night and day this process is ongoing; it is ongoing in every time and every place. It continues across every spot on the surface of the earth. It continues in the atmosphere of the universe, and it continues in the depths of the seas. Permanence belongs only to change in the course of time.

This process is not an ordinary one; it is a miracle. But because we have seen it night and day, we have become so accustomed to it that its miraculous aspect has slipped from our sight, although at every moment the dead is brought forth from the living and the living from the dead, in a new manner and with a new splendour. A dead and dry seed is placed in the earth, and from it come beautiful plants and flowers, and crops grow. When these same fruits, flowers, ears of grain and plants dry out and become chaff, then within that dry chaff thousands of dead seeds have already been prepared, containing complete life within them. These dead seeds again take in the gases, water and warmth of the atmosphere of the universe, and once more come to life. The embryos of humans and animals, and the embryos and eggs of birds, take on the form of life in various shapes and in various measures. This is a continuous cycle: the living becomes dead and the dead becomes living, over and over. Is it difficult for any living and wakeful heart to believe that Allah can recreate? In the light of the Qur'an, understanding this matter is not difficult, because the light of the Qur'an has emerged from the light of Allah.

"Wa kadhalika takhrujun" (30:19): "Just so will you be brought forth." This is a matter that is easy to understand. It is an ordinary and common matter; it is your own observation. Night and day are being seen in the universe. Night and day are being witnessed by you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 30, verse 20:

﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings spreading out [across the earth].﴾ (30:20) Dust is dead and still. Man was created from this very dust. In another place in the Qur'an it is said:

﴿Indeed, We created man from an extract of clay.﴾ (23:12) Dust is in fact the fundamental origin of man. But by mentioning this original substance of human personality here, it is shown that man appears before us in a complete form, walking and moving about. The intent is to say: look at the original material from which man was created, and then look at the fully formed human being, and see how great the difference is between the two. Especially after stating the principle that:

﴿He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living﴾ (30:19), this is, according to the Qur'anic style, a connection of meaning.

This is one of the great signs of the power of Allah. Through its explanation it is intended to show what the relationship is between the human being living on this earth and the earth itself, and what the point is at which they meet, namely from the angle of their original creation and of the laws of divine power that apply both to man himself and to this universe.

That this great transformation within this dead dust is itself a miracle, namely that it changed from a dead and commonplace form into a human being endowed with power and dignity, is a fact in its own right. This is such a transformation and craftsmanship through which the great craftsmanship of Allah, glorified is He, becomes known. The heart and conscience of man spontaneously become inclined to glorify and extol Allah, and man becomes eloquent in praise of this great craftsmanship of Allah, glorified is He. Then the division of human life into male and female comes before us, along with the relationship between these qualities and the subject of shared life. Is this not a miracle no less than an extraordinary, supernatural one?

Among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.

People well know what their feelings are toward the opposite sex. The consciousness and nerves of both kinds are drawn toward one another, and because of their emotions and inclinations they have an overwhelming attraction for each other. These feelings and inclinations drive them to countless tasks and hardships. Yet the inclinations of husband and wife do not turn toward the hand of power of that Wise Being who has done all this. No one even remembers the Creator who placed this attraction and this inclination within these souls. Yet because of this bond between husband and wife, a certain calm, steadiness and seriousness comes into the body, the soul, the nerves, and indeed the whole life of a person, and through this bond a person also derives physical and spiritual pleasure, and this pleasure is equal for both men and women.

Here the Qur'an has adopted a most subtle and delicate manner of expression, and has depicted the relationship of husband and wife in a highly allusive style. It is as though the Qur'an is painting a picture in the depths of the heart and in the layers of feeling and consciousness.

﴿That you may find tranquility in them﴾ (30:21)

﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ (30:21)

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ (30:21). And when they reflect, they will come to know what wisdoms the Creator has placed within the creation of the two sexes: how, in terms of nature, He made each to be complementary and fitting for the other; how each fulfils the natural needs of the other. They stand in relation to one another as completion in psychological, intellectual and physical terms. Each is a place of contentment, stability and tranquility for the other. Through their union completion is achieved, and an independent unit comes into being. Within this unit there is love and mercy, because their physical, psychological, nervous and natural constitution is such that each is incomplete without the other. Man is the place where woman's desires find satisfaction, and woman is the place where man's desires find satisfaction. Thus the unity, harmony and union of the two is the means by which life continues on this earth. Through it the harvest of life is continually renewed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verse 22:

﴿And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (30:22) The creation of the heavens and the earth is a sign to which the Qur'an has repeatedly drawn attention. Yet we live by day and by night upon this earth and beneath this sky, and still we do not reflect upon this creation of God. Whereas the heavens and the earth are worthy of being contemplated for a long time, again and again, and of being pondered deeply.

What is meant by "the creation of the heavens"? It means that God has created this great, intricate and extremely vast universe. Of this great and vast universe we have so far been able to know only a very small part: this immense and countless throng of celestial spheres and orbs, the stars, the planets, their orbits, the galaxies and then black holes. Within this whole universe, our earth is like a tiny particle floating in the atmosphere of our earth, having neither weight nor shadow. Along with the unimaginable vastness of this terrifying universe, it moves on with extremely precise and unchangeable order. In its motions and in the orbits of its spheres there is boundless discipline and order, although the distances between them are enormous. In these motions there is no turbulence and no irregularity, and everything moves according to the command of the Lord.

This observation concerns only the order of the motion of the stars and their spheres. As for the mysteries of this universe, the diverse creatures found within it, their natures, the circumstances in which those creatures live, and the circumstances that befall them, there is no limit to them. Then, the laws that preserve all this creation, that drive it, and that govern it: reaching their final limit is not possible for humans. Human knowledge of all these matters and subjects is very limited; it is not even like a drop from the ocean.

This is a cursory glance at the creation of the heavens and the earth, very briefly. The little knowledge that scientists and anthropologists have acquired in this regard could be discussed at length. According to the information available so far, this universe is very great and its various parts are interconnected. All these parts are in motion since the day of creation without colliding with one another; not for a single second is there any stillness in them. Yet in this wondrous system, which is very intricate, these parts and bodies never collide with one another. Despite the information currently available about this system, some frivolous people dare to say that this universe has no creator, and then that it has no manager who runs it in this way. The nonsense of these so-called scientists is still heard today.

Then, along with the heavens and the earth, there are the people who live in them, namely the different colours, different forms and different languages of humans. This diversity is also connected with the creation of the heavens. The variety of colours and languages on earth is also linked to the creation of the heavens. Colours and languages change according to different regions and seasons. The colour, language, and form and appearance of a human being have a deep connection with meteorology.

The scholars and scientists of our age see the diversity of the colours and languages of people, yet they have never reflected upon it, nor do they come to the realization that these are samples of God's creation and that these matters too are among God's signs. Although they study the diversity of languages very deeply, they do not strive to reach God through considering it as a sign of God. This is why most people, despite claiming that "we are scientists," in reality are not scientists.

﴿They know only an outward aspect of the life of this world﴾ (30:7). And this aspect of humanity and human knowledge, that people's colours differ and their languages differ, can be seen only by true scholars and believing scientists.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those of knowledge﴾ (30:22).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verse 23:

ومن ایتہ منامکم ۔۔۔۔۔۔ لقوم یسمعون (30: 23) ” “۔ In this verse too, cosmic phenomena and the change in human circumstances alongside them are mentioned, and a connection between the two is shown. Through this, a link within these enormous existences becomes apparent, and harmony among them is described. Human sleeping and waking along with the alternation of night and day, and striving in this world for lawful provision (rizq halal), are interconnected. Here lawful provision is expressed as the bounty of God (fadl-e-Ilahi), on the condition that after rest they strive for lawful provision. God has so fashioned this universe that it makes a person's striving easy for him, so that he can live pleasantly on this earth. For this striving He has made the light of day suitable, and for rest and comfort He has made the darkness of night easy. This scene is for most of the creatures living on this earth. Facility has been arranged for each one in graduated measure. In sum, in the order of the universe, every existent finds facility for itself, and these facilities are most natural for it: harmonious with its nature and its life, and pleasant.

ان فی ذلک لایت لقوم یسمعون (30: 23) ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who listen﴾. Sleep is tranquility and striving is movement; both are perceived through hearing. Therefore the word "yasma'un" (who listen) is most fitting according to the mode of expression of the Holy Qur'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verse 24:

ومن ایتہ یریکم ۔۔۔۔۔۔ لایت لقوم یعقلون (30: 24) ” “۔

The flash of lightning is a scene of this cosmic system and of its creation. Some scientists have explained it in this way: lightning exists within clouds. When two pieces of them come together, the collision produces a spark of electricity that agitates the electricity present within the clouds. Or it happens that these clouds strike the peak of a mountain, and this agitation is produced from them, and through it the lightning flashes. Generally, after this flash and collision, rain falls. However, whatever its reality may be, it is a manifestation of the hand of Divine power in this universe, a terrifying manifestation. It is the appearance of those forces and powers which He has deposited in this universe. The Qur'anic method, for the most part, is that it does not discuss the reality of these natural phenomena or their scientific causes, but rather draws from these phenomena only this conclusion: that the heart and mind of a human being, on seeing these phenomena, reach the Creator. Therefore the Holy Qur'an gives from these phenomena only this lesson: that this is one of the signs of Divine power.

ومن ایتہ یریکم البرق خوفا وطمعا (30: 24) ” And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, with fear and also with hope.“ These are the feelings that generally arise in a person with the flash of lightning. A person fears, because it burns humans, animals and crops. Then, on seeing this great power, flash and roar, fear of the forces of this all-encompassing universe arises within a person, and hope arises in that often rain comes with lightning, which is very beneficial for a person. For this reason the Holy Qur'an has mentioned rain along with the flash and roar. وینزل من ۔۔۔۔۔ بعد موتھا (30: 24) ” And He sends down water from the sky and with it gives life to the dead earth after its death.“

By attributing death to the earth and then, after its death, attributing life to it, the impression is given that this earth is in reality alive. It too lives and dies. And in reality it is indeed as the Holy Qur'an depicts it. This earth is in fact a living creation. It submits to the command of Allah. It is obedient and compliant to its Lord, always responding to the commands of its Lord. It is in the servitude of Allah, and this human being who crawls upon this globe is also one of the creatures of Allah. He too proceeds along with this earth under the commands of Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

Moreover, when rain falls upon the earth, greenness and freshness arise within it. Growing crops sprout from it, and they flourish upon its surface. Thus the earth appears alive, in the same way that humans and animals are alive.

ان فی ذلک لایت لقوم یعقلون (30: 24) ” Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.“

﴿And among His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand firm by His command.﴾ (30:25–26)

The arrangement and stability of the heavens and the earth is an extremely sound and firm system, whose movements are fixed, and in which there is not even a second's advance or delay. This is by the planning of Allah, exalted is He. No creature can claim that it, or anyone other than Him, is running this arrangement, and no intelligent person can believe that all this is happening without any planning Doer. If this is so, then what else is it but one of the miracles of Allah? These heavens and earth stand by Allah's establishing them. They carry out Allah's commands; they are His obedient servants. In them there is no disobedience, deviation or disturbance.

﴿Then, when He calls you from the earth, behold, you will come out.﴾ (30:25) Whoever reflects on this system of Allah, and on these measures and powers, can only answer the call of Allah with "Labbayk" (here I am), for when Allah calls, people will come out by themselves through automatic means. Here the discourse on this theme comes to its conclusion, and it is explained that humans, animals, plants and inanimate things are all obedient to Allah.

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.﴾ (30:26) The meaning is that every creature in the heavens and the earth is a servant of Allah, obedient to Him willingly or unwillingly, and all of them proceed in accordance with Allah's sunnah (established way and law). Nothing in them can differ or deviate. All things are subject to Allah's sunnah and will. Whether they are believers or disbelievers in terms of religion, although their hearts and minds may be those of disbelievers, their entire bodies and this whole universe spread around them are obedient to Allah. Just as the other things of the universe are devoutly obedient to the divine sunnah, so too is man. This profound, long and grand journey of the Lord of the universe concludes with the final and important matter: that one day you will be presented before Allah, yet you are heedless of that day.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verse 27:

﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him.﴾ (30:27) Surah 30 has already mentioned the beginning of creation and its repetition. After that long journey and tour of the universe, it is mentioned again here with this addition.

﴿And that is easier for Him.﴾ (30:27) Although nothing is easy or difficult for Allah, this is how the matter stands. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (36:82) That is, when He wills something, He merely says "Be," and it comes to be. However, Allah addresses people in the manner that He knows they can understand. For people, repeating creation is easier than the first creation, yet they go against their own experience and hold that initial creation is easy while repetition is difficult, although repetition should be easier.

﴿And His is the highest similitude in the heavens and the earth.﴾ (30:27) He is unique in the heavens and the earth. There is no partner in His Being or His attributes. There is nothing like Him. He is the One, the Praiseworthy.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (30:27) He is Mighty and Dominant. He does what He wills, and He is Wise; nothing He does is devoid of wisdom. His decree is always firm and complete, perfect and whole. At the conclusion of this great journey of observation, in which we traveled through the horizons and dimensions of this universe, its outward states and its depths, in which we saw scenes and drew out truths, the discourse now strikes its final blow upon the strings of reason and intellect.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 30, verse 28:

Allah has presented you with a parable from your own selves (Qur'an 30:28): "Allah presents to you a parable from yourselves." This parable is not far from your practical life, so that you could fail to grasp it; there is no need to travel to some distant land to observe it.

Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein (Qur'an 30:28)? "Is there any among your slaves who are your partners in the wealth We have bestowed upon you, so that you are equal in it?" It is evident that the polytheists of Makkah did not even wish that their slaves should share in their wealth, let alone that their rights should be equal to their own.

You fear them as you fear one another (Qur'an 30:28): that is, you give them the same standing that you give to your free partners among yourselves. You fear that they will wrong you, and you take care not to wrong them, because they have an equal station with you. Does such a thing happen in your environment and in your own society? After it, there is no further argument on this subject. This parable rests upon a very simple reasoning and sound common sense.

Thus do We make the signs clear for a people who use their reason (Qur'an 30:28): after explaining in detail this feeble contradiction in their beliefs, it is now stated why this contradiction arose in their beliefs and what its real cause is. It is simply that their own desires demand it, and when a person becomes a slave of his carnal desires, he is then deprived of reason and insight.

But those who do wrong follow their desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has sent astray? And for them there are no helpers.

**Lesson No. 184: Overview**

The theme of this surah and this section is the real subject of the surah: there is a deep connection between the events and occurrences of this universe and the values and circumstances of human life. The laws of nature in this universe, the laws of this life, and the laws of this religion, the Shari'ah, are mutually harmonious, coherent, interconnected and free of contradiction.

This lesson shows that human desires keep changing, but there is no change in the Sunnah of Allah (the established way and law of Allah). Shirk-based beliefs have the status of mere tent-pegs when set against the principles of the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim). The lesson then portrays the states of the human soul in different conditions: what the soul is like in a state of security, what it is like in a state of danger, how it behaves when the spirit is constricted (qabd), and what it does when it is expanded (bast). It shows that until a person measures his values and concepts by Allah's standards, his values and his spirit cannot attain stability and tranquility. But when a person turns to Allah, his outlook becomes that it is Allah who expands the provision of some and restricts it for others.

Then it is shown that there is also a firm method for increasing wealth and provision in the world: by what means wealth grows, by what means it diminishes, what makes it pure and what makes it impure. The law of finance too will be correct and upright only if it conforms to the upright religion and is derived from it.

After this, the listeners are turned back and directed toward the One who is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Causer of death. The beings you associate with Allah besides Him cannot do this. It is shown that wherever and whenever shirk exists, it causes corruption. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers are again guided to remain firm on this straight and right religion, and to earn for themselves before the arrival of that Day on which there will be no deed and no earning. There, only the reckoning of deeds will take place.

After this, they are told what provisions Allah has created for them in the world. Some things are for the sustenance of their material life: for example, water falls from the heavens, and the earth becomes alive and green and produces everything for you. Then there are the means of sailing on the seas for you, and for your spiritual life there are these clear signs (ayat bayyinat) being revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by which hearts and minds become alive and flourishing. But alas, people neither take guidance nor listen.

Then it is explained that these people, while living in this world, are going to return to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. On that Day no one's excuse will be accepted, and no requests for forgiveness will be entertained. Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is instructed to continue his task with steadfastness, to be patient until the promise of Allah appears before them. The promise of Allah is certain truth (haqq al-yaqin) and is unalterable.

**Lesson No. 184: Explanation of the Verses (33 to 60)**

﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ النَّاسَ ضُرٌّ دَعَوْا رَبَّهُم مُّنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا أَذَاقَهُم مِّنْهُ رَحْمَةً إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ (30:33)
"When harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord."

﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (30:34)
"So that they may deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know."

This is a psychological portrait of a human being who has not been shaped with firm colours, who does not hold stable values of life, and before whom there is no clear method of living. The soul of such a person wavers between momentary impulses and momentary impressions. Whatever thought comes to mind, he rushes toward it. Because of accidents and passing events, he keeps changing. The condition of such people is that when they are afflicted with difficulties, they remember their Lord and turn toward the true Power, besides which there is no one to save them, and there is no deliverance except by humbly pleading at His court. And when the clouds of difficulty clear, the hardship is removed and the mercy of Allah comes, [they forget].

﴿إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ (30:33) "Then, suddenly, some of them begin to commit shirk." These are the people who do not hold on to sound belief, whose values are not stable. Because the mercies of Allah and the conveniences of the world free them from the hardships which had made them turn toward Allah, they suddenly forget the difficult days in which they used to remember God. Thus they reject the guidance Allah has given and abandon the mercies of Allah, and go toward disbelief, although in the state of mercy, especially after a calamity, they should have remained firm in gratitude and in turning back to Allah (inabah ila Allah).

Such people existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah, in very brief words, swiftly warns them, and they are addressed in this manner. In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), specific individuals were in view; therefore the form of direct address was used.

﴿فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (30:34) "So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know." This is a severe and frightening threat, although it is not direct. A human being is such that he fears even the threat of an ordinary ruler or chief. The threat of Allah, glorified is His majesty, is far more frightening, because nothing is difficult for Allah. Every matter comes into existence by the word "Be!"

﴿فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (30:34) "So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know." After giving this threat swiftly and briefly, they are now seized with harsh indignation regarding their position: that despite Allah's blessings and mercies they commit shirk and adopt the attitude of disbelief. After all, what is their proof for this?

﴿أَمْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانًا فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُوا بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ (30:35) "Have We sent down upon them any authority which speaks of what they have been associating with Him?" Because it is not proper for anyone to take his beliefs and convictions from any source other than Allah. Did We send down any proof in support of shirk? No. This is a strong rebuke and a rhetorical question. It also contains mockery and contempt. The purpose is that their attitude is extremely foolish; there is no argument, no proof, and no authority for it. In other words, it is also a rhetorical question. The meaning is that no belief is established without revelation sent down by Allah. Since Allah has not sent down any proof for shirk, the belief in shirk is false, baseless and weak.

Now another psychological portrait of human beings: when he is prosperous and happy, he becomes frivolous and arrogant.

﴿وَإِذَا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُوا بِهَا وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ﴾ (30:36) "When We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but when an evil befalls them because of what their own hands have sent forth, behold, they fall into despair."

This too is a psychological portrait of a person who does not try to understand the nature of his affairs according to a constant measure. Their attitude is not such that in every condition a single standard and measure remains before them, a standard that never changes. Here the meaning is those people whose values and measures are not constant and lasting. When good days come, they go beyond themselves and forget the One who bestowed these good days, and they remain in the air. They become immersed in luxury and comfort, and do not give thanks to Allah, the true Benefactor, and they do not keep in view that the mercy and prosperity of Allah is also a test. But when, by the will of Allah, calamity comes upon them because of their own wrongdoing, then they display blindness and do not believe that this too is a trial, and that it is a trial of adversity. Therefore they should remember Allah and be patient, that He may remove their difficulties. Instead, they despair and utter nonsense. This portrait is of hearts that are cut off from Allah, who neither know the Sunan of Allah nor understand the wisdom of Allah. These people truly do not know; they are ignorant. They make judgments only by looking at the outward circumstances of life.

After this psychological portrayal, a severe rhetorical question is asked, which also expresses strong astonishment at their situation, and laments their blindness and lack of insight. It is explained that both prosperity and adversity come according to a constant law of nature of Allah. They are connected to the Sunan of Allah and to the will of Allah, because it is He who bestows mercy and He who brings calamity. It is He who expands provision and He who restricts it. Everything happens according to the requirements of His wisdom. In this world events keep happening according to this principle, yet people become blind and do not see.

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ﴾ (30:37) "Do they not see that Allah expands provision for whomever He wills and restricts it?"

Therefore, when provision is expanded, one should not become proud or arrogant. Swelling with pride is not appropriate. And when provision is restricted, one should not despair. These are temporary conditions, which come according to the wisdom of Allah. Through these conditions the heart of the believer comes to be certain that all of this belongs to Allah. The Sunnah of Allah continues to do its work. The system of Allah is constant. Day and night keep changing according to His wisdom.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ (30:37) "Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe."

Since the expansion and restriction of provision are in the sole power of Allah, He is the One who gives and the One who withholds according to His will. Therefore, He shows you which path leads to the progress of your economy, and which economy does not progress, although people regard it as a developing economy. This is guidance.

**Lesson No. 184: Overview**

The theme of this surah and this section is the real subject of the surah: there is a deep connection between the events and occurrences of this universe and the values and circumstances of human life. The laws of nature in this universe, the laws of this life, and the laws of this religion, the Shari'ah, are mutually harmonious, coherent, interconnected and free of contradiction.

This lesson shows that human desires keep changing, but there is no change in the Sunnah of Allah (the established way and law of Allah). Shirk-based beliefs have the status of mere tent-pegs when set against the principles of the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim). The lesson then portrays the states of the human soul in different conditions: what the soul is like in a state of security, what it is like in a state of danger, how it behaves when the spirit is constricted (qabd), and what it does when it is expanded (bast). It shows that until a person measures his values and concepts by Allah's standards, his values and his spirit cannot attain stability and tranquility. But when a person turns to Allah, his outlook becomes that it is Allah who expands the provision of some and restricts it for others.

Then it is shown that there is also a firm method for increasing wealth and provision in the world: by what means wealth grows, by what means it diminishes, what makes it pure and what makes it impure. The law of finance too will be correct and upright only if it conforms to the upright religion and is derived from it.

After this, the listeners are turned back and directed toward the One who is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Causer of death. The beings you associate with Allah besides Him cannot do this. It is shown that wherever and whenever shirk exists, it causes corruption. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers are again guided to remain firm on this straight and right religion, and to earn for themselves before the arrival of that Day on which there will be no deed and no earning. There, only the reckoning of deeds will take place.

After this, they are told what provisions Allah has created for them in the world. Some things are for the sustenance of their material life: for example, water falls from the heavens, and the earth becomes alive and green and produces everything for you. Then there are the means of sailing on the seas for you, and for your spiritual life there are these clear signs (ayat bayyinat) being revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by which hearts and minds become alive and flourishing. But alas, people neither take guidance nor listen.

Then it is explained that these people, while living in this world, are going to return to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. On that Day no one's excuse will be accepted, and no requests for forgiveness will be entertained. Finally, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is instructed to continue his task with steadfastness, to be patient until the promise of Allah appears before them. The promise of Allah is certain truth (haqq al-yaqin) and is unalterable.

"So that they may deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know."

The soul of such a person wavers between momentary impulses and momentary impressions. Whatever thought comes to mind, he rushes toward it. Because of accidents and passing events, he keeps changing. The condition of such people is that when they are afflicted with difficulties, they remember their Lord and turn toward the true Power, besides which there is no one to save them, and there is no deliverance except by humbly pleading at His court. Because the mercies of Allah and the conveniences of the world free them from the hardships which had made them turn toward Allah, they suddenly forget the difficult days in which they used to remember God. Such people existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah, in very brief words, swiftly warns them, and they are addressed in this manner. In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), specific individuals were in view; therefore the form of direct address was used.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 38–39:

فات ذا القربی ۔۔۔۔۔ ھم المضعفون (38 – 39)

Since the concept is that all wealth belongs to Allah, and Allah has given some of His servants more and some less, according to this concept Allah, the First Owner of all wealth, commands that wealth should continually be transferred to those who are needy. This is why Allah has called it the right of the needy. Here, some specific groups among these needy are also mentioned.

"So give to the near of kin, and the needy, and the wayfarer" (30:38). At the time this verse was revealed, zakah had not yet been fixed, nor had the categories of its recipients been specified. In principle, it was established that all wealth truly belongs to Allah, since the Provider is Allah. The needy have a fixed right in this wealth, and this right has been granted by the true owner of the wealth. This right reaches them through the person in whose hands the wealth is accumulated. This is the fundamental view of Islam regarding wealth. The foundation of Islam's economic and financial principles is this very concept, that the true owner is Allah. When wealth belongs to Allah, the obligations imposed by Allah must be fulfilled first. Whether Allah's commands concern ownership, or commands concerning growth and warning, or commands concerning spending, all of these are binding commands, and the one who holds wealth is not free to dispose of his wealth as he wishes.

Now, Allah guides those to whom He has entrusted this wealth as a trust: by what method will you increase and develop this wealth? The method of increase is that it be spent on relatives, travellers and the needy. All of this is spent in the way of Allah.

"That is better for those who desire the Countenance of Allah, and it is those who are the successful" (30:38). Some people used to give their wealth as gifts to wealthy people so that they would return more in response to the gift, double or triple. Allah made clear that this is not the method of increasing wealth.

"And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah" (30:39). Traditions have stated this to be the meaning of this verse. However, the text of the Qur'an is general, and all usurious transactions through which people seek to increase their wealth fall under it, whatever their form may be. Instead of the increase of wealth through usury, it has been explained what the true form of growth is.

"And whatever zakah you give, seeking the Countenance of Allah, it is those who are the multipliers" (30:39). This is the means and method that is the certain way of increasing wealth. That is, give wealth freely, do not await any return reward, and let there be no compensation. Spend purely for the sake of Allah and for the sake of Allah's countenance, because it is Allah who grants expansiveness in provision and who also constricts provision. The Giver and the Withholder is He alone. Those who spend for Allah, He gives them many times over, and those who spend seeking the approval of people, He diminishes their wealth. This usurious business is the arrangement of the world, and that is the reckoning of the Hereafter, and in it wealth is received many times over. This is the profitable trade, here and there. Now, from the perspective of provision and earning, the issue of shirk is taken up. The traces of shirk among present-day people and the traces of shirk among earlier nations are described.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 40–41:

ﷲ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم ۔۔۔۔۔ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّشْرِكِينَ (40 – 42)

Allah sets before them the true reality of their own lives, and presents to them circumstances about which they have no doubt that Allah is their originator, or circumstances about which they cannot claim that their supposed gods and deities originated them or share in them. It is Allah who created you; He is the One who provides for you, He is the One who causes you to die, and He is the One who will bring you back to life. As far as creation is concerned, they acknowledged it. As far as provision is concerned, they could not claim that their supposed deities provide for them. As for death, they could claim nothing except that Allah is the One who causes death. As for the matter of resurrection after death, they did doubt it. Allah, the Exalted, places resurrection after death among the things they accept, in the list of accepted matters, so that their consciousness may awaken, and thus they may be convinced of it. This is a direct address to their nature and their innate perception. Although a deviation had entered their natural way of thinking, if nature is left to face the real circumstances and a person thinks in a natural manner, then there is no alternative to the belief in resurrection after death. Allah then asks them:

هَلْ مِن شُرَكَائِكُم ۔۔۔۔۔ مِن شَيْءٍ (30: 40) "Is there any among your associates who does any of these things?" The answer to this question is not awaited, because it is a question meant for refutation and also for reproach, and it does not require an answer. Right after it, it is simply declared that Allah is free of such associates.

سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (30: 40) "Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him."

After this, it is explained that the reform and corruption of human life in the world are connected with the deeds of people. When people's hearts become corrupted, their deeds become bad and their beliefs become bad, this causes disorder in the earthly system, and both land and sea are caught in this corruption. This corruption comes to dominate the values of people's lives.

ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ ۔۔۔۔۔ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ (30: 41) "Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned." The emergence of corruption in the system of the world and its spreading is not without purpose, nor does it happen suddenly by chance. It occurs according to Allah's providence and His laws of nature.

لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا (30: 41) "So that He may let them taste some of what they have done." That is, when they are engaged in deeds that cause evil and corruption, and when they are caught in this general corruption and feel its burning and heat, the possibility arises...

لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (30: 41) "Perhaps they will return." And resolve that they will confront this corruption, turn back to Allah, begin righteous deeds, and adopt the straight and correct system of life. At the end of this lesson, they are warned of the fate that befell the polytheists of earlier times. The people of Makkah were also acquainted with the fate of most of them, because they would see their traces during their journeys. These traces were upon the clear path.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 43–45:**

*Fa-aqim wajhaka lid-din...* ... *innahu la yuhibbul-kafirin* (43–45)

The image the Qur'an prescribes for one who turns toward the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim) is extraordinarily striking, and it shows that the one who turns has turned to it with his whole attention. He is earnest and upright.

*Fa-aqim wajhaka lid-dinil-qayyim* (30:43): "Set your face firmly toward the upright religion." With the utmost attentiveness and full focus, like one awaiting the command, turn your face firmly toward the Higher World, in the way a soldier stands at attention (at-tenshun). The command to set one's face toward the upright religion came for the first time in this surah at a point where the subject was people following their base desires and various factions running in different directions. Here the command comes in opposition to the associators (shuraka'). It comes in the context of the increase of provision (rizq). It comes in the context of corruption spreading across the world because of shirk and because of people's bad conduct. After this it is stated that whoever does righteous deeds will reap a good fruit, and whoever does evil deeds will have an evil end. That day will be one in which people will be divided into two parties, the people of faith and the people of disbelief, each will have its own outcome, and that day will be certain.

*Man kafara fa-'alayhi kufruhu wa man 'amila salihan fa-li-anfusihim yamhadun* (30:44): "Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief, and those who have done righteous deeds are preparing (a path of success) for themselves." Yamhadun means: to prepare, to bring under control, to prepare a cradle in which a child rests comfortably, to prepare a path, to prepare a bed on which one rests. All these meanings convey that one smooths out something for oneself. Through *yamhadun* the nature and character of righteous action and its results are revealed. Those who do righteous deeds are in fact preparing for themselves an environment of comfort, pleasantness and joy; that is, even in the state of action they receive these results, while what comes later is another matter. The Qur'anic manner of expression through *yamhadun* makes this clear.

*Liyajziyal-ladhina amanu wa 'amilus-salihati min fadlihi* (30:45): "That Allah may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty." To be rewarded out of His bounty means that no person can deserve Paradise solely on the basis of his deeds. However many deeds a person performs, he cannot render thanks for even a single small favour of Allah through them. Paradise can be attained only through the bounty of the Lord. Allah, glory be to Him, greatly dislikes the disbelievers.

*Innahu la yuhibbul-kafirin* (30:45): Now, here some of Allah's signs are shown. Along with being signs of Allah, they are also favour and mercy for mankind. Through these signs provision is supplied to people. This is guidance for them, but they recognise some of Allah's signs and deny others.
