Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 46–51:

ومن ایتہ ان یرسل ۔۔۔۔۔ من بعدہ یکفرون (46 – 51)

In these verses, subjects of very different kinds have been brought together. Winds that bring good tidings, the sending of Messengers with miracles and signs, the help of the believers through the Messengers, the descent of rains that revive dead land, and the question of resurrection after death. This gathering has a purpose. All of these things are signs of Allah's mercy. All of them are manifestations of the Sunnah of Allah (sunnat-i-ilahiyyah), all of them operate under the system of this universe, there is a deep connection between the sending of Messengers with guidance and the help given to the believers, and all of them are different examples of the signs of Allah (ayat-i-ilahiyyah). All these matters relate to the blessings and mercies of Allah. The life of people depends upon all these matters, and all these matters are connected with the system of the universe.

ومن ایتہ یرسل الریاح مبشرت (30:46) "And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news." These winds carry and spread the rains. The people of that time knew well the winds that bring rain. They had skill and experience in this matter. When such winds blew, these people rejoiced.

ولیذیقکم من رحمتہ (30:46) "So that He may let you taste of His mercy." As a result of this mercy there is greenness, freshness and growth.

ولتجری الفلک بامرہ (30:46) "So that ships may sail by His command." These ships sail both in the sense that these winds drive them, and in the sense that through the winds rain falls, rivers flow, and ships sail in them. They sail by the command of Allah despite these apparent causes, in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah by which He created this universe, and in accordance with the system of His decree by which He has determined a property within every thing. For example, the ship was made light on the surface of the water so that it began to move; and the ship moves in the direction of the wind and waves, and against their direction. Allah has made everything according to a measure.

ولتبتغوا من فضلہ (30:46) "So that you may seek His bounty." That is, in commercial journeys and in the harvest, in giving and taking; all these affairs are by the bounty of Allah, and Allah has created everything according to a measure... in full.

ولعلکم تشکرون (30:46) "So that you may be grateful." All these matters are the bounty of Allah, and you should be grateful for them. All these matters are such that it is the duty of the servants of Allah to adopt an appropriate attitude toward these blessings of Allah. Just as the sending of winds, the sending of Messengers is also a bounty and grace of Allah upon mankind.

ولقد ارسلنا ۔۔۔۔ بالبینت (30:47) "And We certainly sent Messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear signs." But people did not await this mercy of Allah, although this mercy was such that they should have welcomed it even more than the winds. These people did not benefit from the Messengers, although this benefit was greater and lasting, compared to the benefits of rain and water. And people divided themselves in regard to the Messengers. One group was of those criminals who did not believe, did not reflect upon the signs of Allah, did not hesitate to harm the Messengers, and did not refrain from the crime of barring people from the path of Allah. The second group was of those believers who understood the signs of Allah, gave thanks to Allah, trusted in the promises of Allah, and bore great torments at the hands of those criminals. Thus the outcome was what accorded with the justice of Allah, and the promise of Allah is always firm.

فانتقمنا من الذین ۔۔۔۔۔ نصر المومنین (30:47) "So We took vengeance upon those who committed crimes, and it was upon Us to help the believers." Holy is He who made the help of the believers obligatory upon Himself, and declared it to be their right rather than a mere favour upon them. He confirmed it in such a manner and made it binding such that there remained no doubt in this help; and how could there be doubt when the one promising is Allah, who is Strong, Mighty and Compelling. He is Exalted, controls His servants, and is All-Wise and All-Aware. This is Allah who says, whose will is never rejected, and whose Sunnah is never changed, because His law of nature operates throughout this entire universe.

Sometimes this help appears to come late, but this delay is according to the measures of human beings, because people reckon matters by their own measures, not by the measures of Allah. They do not assess matters by the assessments of Allah, and Allah is All-Wise and All-Aware. He knows what the right time for help is. His promise comes true at the time that is in accordance with His will and the requirement of His wisdom. Sometimes the wisdom of the time that Allah fixes is known to people, and sometimes it is not known; but what Allah wills is always the best, and the time Allah fixes is always the right one. But the promise of Allah is certain and is the certainty of certainty, and those who are patient and rely upon Him await it with great tranquillity.

After this it is said that it is Allah who sends the winds, who bring rain by which the earth is made alive after it had died. In the same way will be the raising of people on the Day of Gathering. Exactly in this way will it be. People will emerge from the earth as the crop springs up. These two are natural laws of this universe.

اللہ الذی یرسل الریع (30:48) "It is Allah who sends the winds." These winds move according to His law of nature, and this law is firmly operative in this universe.

فتثیر سحابا (30:48) "Then they raise clouds." These winds lift the vapours of water and spread them in the heavens. فیبسطہ فی السمآء کیف یشآء (30:48) "Then He spreads them in the sky however He wills."

ویجعلہ کسفا (30:48) "And He makes them into fragments." That is, He gathers them. They become dense and heavy, and they settle in layers above and below one another. Some clouds collide with others. Then lightning flashes. فتری الودق یخرج من خللہ (30:48) "Then you see the rain drops coming out from between them." Wadq means the rain that comes out of the clouds.

فاذزا اصاب ۔۔۔۔۔ یستبشرون (30:48) "When He lets it fall upon whomever of His servants He wills, behold, they rejoice." This joy can be best understood by those whose lives depend upon rain. The Arabs were well acquainted with this scene, whose entire livelihood depended, and still depends, upon the waters of the heavens, and they mention it with great affection in their poetry, their traditions and their idioms, with great pride and boasting.

وان کانوا من۔۔۔۔۔ قبلہ لمبلسین (30:49) "Although before it was sent down they were despairing." This was their condition when rain had not fallen. They despaired and thought that they were about to die. But when the rain comes, they rejoice.

فانظر الی اثر رحمت اللہ (30:50) "Look, then, at the effects of Allah's mercy." Look at those joyful faces who had become completely despairing, and look at the signs upon this earth which was ruined and dead. And look at the life that moves upon the earth, and look at the hopes that arise in people's hearts out of joy.

یحی الارض بعد موتھا (30:50) "How He revives the earth after its death." This is a reality that every person can see. To see it, no great intellect is required. This very thing is a clear proof that on the Day of Resurrection human beings will rise from this earth in the same way. This is the intuitive mode of argument of the Holy Qur'an, that it establishes beliefs and future events and possibilities from the observable scenes of this universe. The Qur'an proves its purpose from these commonplace scenes.

ان ذلک ۔۔۔۔۔ شئ قدیر (30:50) "Indeed, He is the one who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Competent." These signs of Allah's mercy upon this earth show that Allah's promise is true, that He will raise people up, and that there will be a good or bad end for them, according to the promise of Allah.

After this depiction of the reality, it is explained that those people rejoice at the arrival of winds bringing clouds laden with water, and when they see the signs of Allah's mercy in the form of clouds and rain, they rejoice. If these same people were to see that these winds and clouds are yellow, and that these winds carry hot sand and dust instead of water, without a single drop of water, and that this wind is such that it turns crops yellow and dries up milk-giving animals, and that the harvest, turned yellow, dries up before its time and becomes chaff, then their condition is this:

ولئن ارسلنا ۔۔۔۔۔ بعدہ یکفرون (30:51) "And if We send a wind and they see their crop turned yellow, they would persist in disbelief after it." Even on finding themselves in such torment and despair, they would still disbelieve, would not acknowledge the power of Allah, would not beseech Allah to remove this calamity, but would remain fixed in the attitude of disbelief, would not believe, and would not understand what the wisdom and planning of Allah accomplish. They would not see the hand of divine power behind these calamities. They would not interpret these events and incidents as happening in accordance with the law of nature and the natural order established by Allah. Rather, they make eternal disbelieving interpretations. When people reach the point where they interpret the events and incidents of this world according to their own desires, and do not even strive to understand the signs and indications of Allah hidden within those events, and do not reflect upon their surroundings, and in these observations do not perceive the power and wisdom of Allah, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is told that he is excused from guiding such people. Leave such people to their own temperament, for their insight and their sight have both been destroyed.

ویجعلہ کسفا (30:48) "And He makes them into fragments." That is, He gathers them. They become dense and heavy, and they settle in layers above and below one another. Some clouds collide with others. Look at those joyful faces who had become completely despairing, and look at the signs upon this earth which was ruined and dead. And look at the life that moves upon the earth, and look at the hopes that arise in people's hearts out of joy.

They would not see the hand of divine power behind these calamities. **Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 52–53:**

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear . . . and they are Muslims﴾ (52–53)

These people are dead. There is no spark of life in them. They are deaf and cannot hear any voice. They are blind and see nothing at all. A person who closes the doors of his perception to this universe, to the laws of nature (nawamis-i-fitrat), and who does not see these signs of nature, has died. There is no life in him. If there is any life in him, it is animal life, and he is even more misguided than animals. Animals have a natural consciousness, and that consciousness never makes a mistake. A person who does not hear the call of Allah's signs is completely deaf, even if he has ears and sound strikes them. A person who does not see Allah's signs scattered throughout this universe is blind, even if he has large, prominent eyes like an animal.

﴿You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, and they are the ones who submit﴾ (30:53). Only such people hear the call, because their hearts are alive, and life truly means the life of the heart. Their eyes are sighted, and their faculties of perception are sound and intact, so they hear. They bow in submission. As soon as the call of the Da'wah strikes their nature, it awakens repentance (inabat) within them.

Now, let man be taken on a tour of his own self and of the world of his body. He is brought out of his surroundings and made to wander through the valleys of his own soul, so that he may consider: How were you created? What is your creation on this earth like? What is life like, and how do you die? And then, what will the scene of the Resurrection be?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 54–57:

اللہ الذی خلقکم ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ معذرتھم ولا ھم یستعتبون (54–57) This is a very long journey of reflection. It begins with the beginning of human life, which lies before us and is an observation of every day. Its final part, though not widely known, the Qur'an depicts in such words that it seems to be before our eyes. This is a journey of reflection in which there is a lesson for those who have seeing eyes, open ears, and those who listen attentively.

اللہ الذی خلقکم من ضعف (30:54) "It is Allah who created you from weakness" (Allah is He who created you from a state of weakness). He said "created you from weakness," not "created you weak." This indicates that the element at the beginning of their life is weakness. The weakness referred to here has many meanings and manifestations, and these manifestations are observable in a human being, and more observations keep coming. That tiny cell from which the embryo forms is very microscopic and small and weak. Then the embryo and all its stages are a state of weakness. Then the whole period of childhood is a state of weakness, until a human becomes a complete youth. Then the material from which a human is made is weak: clay. If there were not the breathing of spirit (nafkh-i-zabani) in it, it would have remained clay, or would have been plants or animals, all of which are weak in comparison to a human. Then a human is weak before his desires; tests and inclinations compel him. If there were not the breathing of the spirit from Allah, a human would not be in this "best of forms," would not have these capacities, and would be, like other animals, a weak and helpless creature.

ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوۃ (30:54) "Then after weakness He gave you strength." Strength of such a kind, and in the same senses in which weakness was described: physical strength, strength in human structure, a person's psychological and spiritual strength, and a person's intellectual and rational strength.

ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوۃ ضعفا وشیبۃ (30:54) "Then after that strength He made you weak and aged." The human body becomes loose; old age is in fact a return, in all of a person's powers, toward childhood. Sometimes psychological decline also sets in, and a person becomes weak of will. Sometimes an old man speaks meaningless words just as a child does. There is no strength in his resolve. With old age, the whiteness of the hair in fact embodies old age, and with the whiteness of hair the weakness of human faculties appears before the eyes. These stages, which no perishable thing can escape, and which a person granted long life never fails to pass through, never happen in a way that any of them fails to come at its appointed time. That these stages come upon every person in this same order is a sign that this human being is under the control of an all-governing Being. That Being creates what it wills, decrees what it wills, and plans for every creature its circumstances and ways in whatever manner it wills. All these affairs are carried out according to Allah's firm knowledge, His decree, and profound technology.

یخلق ما یشآء وھو العلیم القدیر (30:54) "He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful." Therefore this creation, made according to such a firm, technical, and designed plan, has a meaningful end. Indeed, it has a most meaningful end and philosophy, and see it in a scene, one of the most impactful scenes of the Day of Resurrection, which is presented through movement and dialogues in every scene.

ویوم تقوم الساعۃ ۔۔۔۔۔ غیر ساعۃ (30:55) "On the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they remained no more than an hour." In their perception, the whole span of time spent in the world will shrink. Therefore they will swear according to their perception. It is also possible that they are saying this about the time spent in graves: that this period was so brief. It is also possible that what is meant is the entire period, that is, the life of the earth and then staying in the graves.

کذلک ۔۔۔۔ یوفکون (30:55) "Thus they used to be deluded in the life of the world." They turned away from the truth, and in the world they had not correctly assessed events. Accordingly, people of knowledge and people of faith will correct their notion.

وقال الذین ۔۔۔۔۔ کنتم لا تعلمون (30:56) "But those who were given knowledge and faith will say: by Allah's Book you have remained until the Day of Resurrection, so this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know." Those people of knowledge and insight were the ones who had faith, and who had believed in the Gathering. They had also come to know the realities behind this apparent world. These people too entrust the matter to Allah's knowledge.

لقد لبثتم ۔۔۔۔۔ یوم البعث (30:56) "Indeed you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection." This is the appointed term. It makes no difference how long it took you to reach the Gathering. This was the appointed day, and here it has come; see.

Now this scene ends in the form of a general principle, and it describes what circumstances are about to befall the wrongdoers who denied the Gathering and the Hour.

فیومئذ لا ینفع ۔۔۔۔۔ یستعتبون (30:57) "So on that day, their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, nor will they be asked to seek forgiveness." Neither will their excuse be accepted, nor will anyone rebuke them by asking why they did such and such. "Seek forgiveness, repent, for today there is punishment; here no one will be reproached. This is the Day of Requital, not the Day of Reproach." Now, bringing them back from this grim and despairing scene, they are returned to the state in which they were, fearful in their obstinacy and denial. This was the end of obstinacy, and this was the conclusion of denial.

Those people of knowledge and insight were the ones who had faith, and who had believed in the Gathering. They had also come to know the realities behind this apparent world. These people too entrust the matter to Allah's knowledge.

لقد لبثتم ۔۔۔۔۔ یوم البعث (30:56) "Indeed you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection." This is the appointed term. It makes no difference how long it took you to reach the Gathering. This was the appointed day, and here it has come; see.

Now this scene ends in the form of a general principle, and it describes what circumstances are about to befall the wrongdoers who denied the Gathering and the Hour.

فیومئذ لا ینفع ۔۔۔۔۔ یستعتبون (30:57) "So on that day, their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, nor will they be asked to seek forgiveness." Neither will their excuse be accepted, nor will anyone rebuke them by asking why they did such and such. "Seek forgiveness, repent, for today there is punishment; here no one will be reproached. This is the Day of Requital, not the Day of Reproach." Now, bringing them back from this grim and despairing scene, they are returned to the state in which they were, fearful in their obstinacy and denial. This was the end of obstinacy, and this was the conclusion of denial.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 30, verses 58–60:

ولقد ضربنا للناس ۔۔۔۔۔۔ لا یعلمون (58 – 59)

There is a sudden change in the context of the discourse and in the time and place of the addressees. This is a far-reaching shift, yet here the distances are gathered together, and the position on which we now stand appears very near. Once again we are before the Qur'an, hearing its sublime examples. Before us are the varied and diverse modes of speech of the Qur'an, in which every colour, every style and every method is employed to make its message settle in hearts, and within which there come countless moments that leave deep impressions upon a human being. The Qur'an addresses every heart and speaks to every level of intellect. Its discourses with every society and every civilisation are according to the capacity of people. It addresses the human self in its various conditions, and it takes up every state and every manner of human conduct and circumstance. But despite these all-embracing and comprehensive efforts, people remain bent upon denial. And they do not limit themselves to denying the signs and verses of Allah; rather, these people also lay hands upon those who possess true knowledge, and in reverse they accuse them of being people of falsehood.

لئن جئتھم بایۃ ۔۔۔۔۔ الا مبطلون (30: 58) "Even if you bring them any sign, those who have refused to believe will say, 'You are only upon falsehood.'" Then comes this remark upon their tongues:

کذلک یطبع اللہ علی قلوب الذین لا یعلمون (30: 58) "Thus does Allah set a seal upon the hearts of those who do not know." "Thus" means according to this method and for these reasons. Those who do not know, their hearts have been sealed. Their inner vision does not open to see the signs and the marks of Allah. These people lay hands upon the people of knowledge and the people of guidance. This is why they have become deserving that Allah distorts their insight and stamps their hearts, because Allah, glorified is He, knows well what is in these hearts and He sees their insights well. In this Surah, after the dialogue with the polytheists, the contemplation of this universe, the study of human history, and the contemplation of human personality, human life and its growth, and after all the evidences and signs have been seen, and even after observing some people who do not believe at all, this is now the final blow upon the strings of reason and intellect. Through it, the believers and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are guided that

فاصبر ان وعد ۔۔۔۔۔ لا یوقنون (60)

"So be patient (O Prophet ﷺ); indeed the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you light (of heart)." In this long struggle and the arduous journey of the Islamic revolution, patience is the means of the believers. This journey is so long and so difficult that at times a person sees it as endless. But one must have certainty in the promise of Allah. To remain fixed upon one's goal without any restlessness, any wavering, and without any bewilderment or anxiety is itself the provision for this path. Showing patience and steadfastness at a time when others are faltering, when some deny and begin to doubt Allah's promise, is required. This is because those who doubt lack the causes of certainty. As for those who have reached Allah and who have held firmly to the rope of Allah, their method is the method of patience and steadfastness, even if the road becomes long, even if its outcome is hidden from sight, and even if it is veiled behind dust and clouds.

This Surah ends in the way it began: its opening theme was that the defeated Romans would, according to Allah's promise, achieve victory after a few years, and at the same time the believers would also attain victory. Its conclusion rests on the theme that if you act with patience and steadfastness, Allah's promise will certainly be fulfilled, for Allah supports those who believe. Moreover, when people strive to discredit this movement and to sow doubts within its ranks, and these are the very people who are enemies of the Islamic movement and do not believe in this new call, then in such circumstances patience is the weapon of the believers. Thus the beginning and the end of the Surah come into harmony. In this way the Surah concludes, and it leaves in the mind of a sincere reader a strong hope that if patience and steadfastness are practised, Allah's promise will surely be fulfilled. Allah's promise is true, and He does not break faith with those who have certainty.
